theses.thesis: Agents are becoming a new privileged-identity class, and employee-account agents just inherited every permission a human never should have delegated.
theses.why_now: This week's news shows the shift landing all at once: AI agents now run under employees' own accounts, and the OS is responding — Apple is tightening macOS Full Disk Access specifically because of agent risk.
evidence: Rig Security launches with $12M to watch AI agents that run under employees' accounts
Apple says it's tightening macOS 'Full Disk Access' controls due to new risks from AI agents
AI agent identity security demands layered defenses, Omdia says
theses.angle: Don't build another scanner — build the runtime identity plane: per-agent scoped credentials, action-level attestation, and least-privilege shells that agents can't escape. The wedge is being the broker between the agent and every tool it touches, like an IAM layer purpose-built for non-human actors.

theses.thesis: The inference war is over and the agent-infrastructure war just started: tokens are commoditized, so the money is moving to stateful 'full computers for agents'.
theses.why_now: Modal is simultaneously raising a $750M round at $15.75B valuation, shipping GA clusters, and launching VM sandboxes pitched as 'full computers for agents' — while CoreWeave and NetApp/Nvidia reframe the bottleneck as wiring, power, and storage rather than raw FLOPs.
evidence: VM Sandboxes: Full computers for agents
Source: Inference provider Modal Labs closing in on $750M round at $15.75B valuation
Wiring and powering GPUs differently can swing AI latency by orders of magnitude, says CoreWeave
theses.angle: Attack the agent-state layer: checkpoint/restore for long-running agent sessions, persistent memory and file systems, and reproducible sandbox images. Whoever owns cheap, instant, stateful agent sandboxes becomes the AWS-of-agents; the pure token API is a race to zero margin.

theses.thesis: Orbital compute is splitting into two opposite bets — megawatt space data centers vs. inference on the satellite itself — and both need an orchestration layer that doesn't exist yet.
theses.why_now: Google's own math says SpaceX needs 1,600 Starship launches before orbital data centers pencil out, while Satlyt just raised $8M to run AI models on satellites in orbit — the edge and the mega-DC are being built in parallel with no common software stack.
evidence: Google thinks SpaceX's Starship has to launch 1,600 times before space data centers get off the ground
Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raises $8M to run AI on satellites
Satellite software provider Satlyt closes $8M investment
theses.angle: Build the 'Kubernetes for orbit': a scheduler that handles radiation-hardened hardware, intermittent downlinks, thermal/power budgets, and workload migration between satellite edge and ground. Sell to the constellation operators who are all about to reinvent this wheel badly.

theses.thesis: AI funding has bifurcated: mega-rounds concentrate in infrastructure with real revenue while application-layer startups compete for a shrinking pool of seed checks.
theses.why_now: Modal raised $750M at a $15.75B valuation, Manus raised $500M+ at $4B, and Arena nearly doubled to $3.1B in ten months — all picks-and-shovels — while Seattle startups raised a record $3.5B even as national VC funding cools.
evidence: AI agent developer Manus raises $500M+ at reported $4B valuation
Popular AI leaderboard Arena nearly doubles valuation to $3.1B valuation in 10 months
Rocket fuel: Seattle-area startups raise a record $3.5B as national VC funding cools
theses.angle: If you're raising, sell shovels or show revenue: infra and eval-layer startups price like infrastructure, while pure application plays need a 10x efficiency story to clear the bar.

theses.thesis: The top AI talent trade is no longer hiring individuals but acquiring entire research teams — AMD's $8.2B World Labs deal set the template.
theses.why_now: AMD is acquiring Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion, a 19-year-old founder just raised $10M for his next startup, and new services now match businesses with AI founders for hire — team-level talent is being priced like an asset class.
evidence: AMD will acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 billion
Cal AI's 19-year-old founder just raised $10M for his new AI startup
AI founders for hire: Startup hub Foundations launches service to connect businesses with builders
theses.angle: Build the infrastructure for team-level talent markets: acqui-hire deal flow, research-team spinout tooling, or retention products for labs watching their stars get poached.

theses.thesis: Distribution and eval mindshare now price like infrastructure: Arena's $3.1B valuation says the leaderboard is the asset, not just the models on it.
theses.why_now: Arena nearly doubled its valuation to $3.1B in ten months without training a frontier model, while Liquid AI pushes device-level personal models and Goodfire ships cheaper agent monitors — value is migrating to the measurement layer.
evidence: Popular AI leaderboard Arena nearly doubles valuation to $3.1B valuation in 10 months
Liquid AI builds personal AI around device-level context
Goodfire says its new 'inside-out' monitors catch rogue AI agents at a fraction of the cost
theses.angle: Be the arena, not the gladiator: eval infrastructure, domain-specific leaderboards, and trust layers monetize every model cycle regardless of which lab wins.

theses.thesis: Inference is being repriced from tokens to outcomes: decentralized marketplaces and 90%-cheaper serving stacks are collapsing the per-token price umbrella.
theses.why_now: Antseed launched a decentralized inference marketplace to slash developer costs, Anyscale published a recipe cutting coding-agent serving costs by 90%, and Goodfire caught rogue agents at a fraction of the cost — three independent cost collapses in a single week.
evidence: Antseed launches a decentralized marketplace for AI inference that dramatically lowers developers' costs
Cut coding agent costs by 90%: Secure LLM serving with Ray + vLLM on Anyscale
Goodfire says its new 'inside-out' monitors catch rogue AI agents at a fraction of the cost
theses.angle: Build on the collapse: applications that were uneconomical at last year's token prices now pencil out — arbitrage the spread before the price umbrella fully falls.
